statement: The Akan supreme being carries multiple names/praise-titles used contextually rather than as fully interchangeable synonyms: Onyame (basic term for Deity), Onyankopon ("the one who alone is great/Supreme One"), Odomankoma ("the Infinite/Interminable One," creator epithet), and Borebore ("carver/excavator/originator"). Source: J.B. Danquah's own tripartite distinction (The Akan Doctrine of God, 1944/2nd ed. 1968).

sources.citation: Danquah, J.B. The Akan Doctrine of God: A Fragment of Gold Coast Ethics and Religion. 2nd ed., Frank Cass, 1968 (orig. 1944).
sources.author: J.B. Danquah

notes: Danquah (1895-1965) was himself an anticolonial lawyer/philosopher/politician (co-founder UGCC, died in Nkrumah-era detention), not a neutral ethnographer — per "Joseph B. Danquah's The Akan Doctrine of God (1944): Anticolonial Fragments?", Fighting Words, Peter Lang, 2017, he used monotheism/Greek philosophical categories as his comparative benchmark, underwriting a "Ghana hypothesis" for postcolonial Akan/Ghanaian identity — read as a documented early-20th-century interpretive/political source, not neutral description.
